title: Employment Situation, February 2027 (BLS, 08:30 ET) — an ordinary first-Friday release, and the second of the two payrolls between the January and March FOMC meetings
source: EST: derived from BLS's own scheduling rule — release on the third Friday following the end of the reference week, the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th. The rule was re-implemented from scratch by the never-assessed research of jobs-2027-01-08 on 2026-09-09 and validated against BLS PRIMARIES rather than against sibling ledgers: 102 of 106 primary-dated reference months reproduce exactly, from BLS's own historical release-date table (bls.gov/bls/histreleasedates.pdf, 1957-2000, parsed deterministically) and its current schedule page (bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm, fetched 2026-09-09, covering Nov 2025 through Nov 2026); the four disagreements are the 1995-96 and 2025 shutdown displacements plus one unexplained 1998-11-05 pull-forward. February 2027's 12th is a FRIDAY, so the reference week is Sun 2027-02-07 to Sat 2027-02-13 and the third Friday after 02-13 is 2027-03-05. NEITHER DOCUMENTED CORRECTION APPLIES: this is not a December reference month, so the January-4 boundary that produces the proposer's own slipped date is irrelevant here, and 2027-03-05 is not a federal holiday, so the Independence-Day pull-forward is irrelevant too. It is an ordinary NYSE trading day. Prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov has published no 2027 schedule at all — /schedule/news_release/2027_sched.htm returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-09 — and a derived date is not a published one. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of jobs-2027-01-08, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED, NOT CANONICAL. Filed to close a GAP the proposer's own proposal named and measured, not merely an adjacency: canonical jobs-* entries run 2026-09-04, 2026-10-02, 2026-11-06, 2026-12-04 and then jump to 2027-05-07, leaving every Employment Situation from January to April 2027 untracked. jobs-2027-01-08 is canonical as of this PR; jobs-2027-02-05 is already proposed by the treasury-refunding-2027-02-03 lane and is deliberately NOT re-proposed here (a competing proposal buys nothing and the scanner warns on it); this file and its sibling jobs-2027-04-02.from-jobs-2027-01-08.json close the remaining two, so the January-April 2027 hole is fully covered. WHY IT IS WORTH TRACKING: from federalreserve.gov's own 2027 calendar (HTTP 200, page-stated 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'), the 2027 FOMC meets January 26-27 and then March 16-17 with a Summary of Economic Projections; this print and jobs-2027-02-05 are the only two payrolls between them, making this the LAST labour print the March SEP meeting sees. HONEST LIMITS: the date is derived, not published, and the derivation's own validation set is 1993-2000 plus 2025-11..2026-08 — the 2001-2024 stretch is reproduced by the corrected rule but was not primary-checked month by month. Re-check once bls.gov publishes a 2027 schedule, normally in the autumn of the preceding year. Note for sibling lanes: bls.gov returns HTTP 403 to curl from this runner on every route, but SERVES the same pages to WebFetch — the schedule page, the historical release-date PDF and individual archive releases were all retrieved that way on 2026-09-09, which is the first successful BLS retrieval this lane has recorded. symbols: [] and status estimate: nothing here licenses an entry.
